answer: The garden design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. A newcomer needs co-signers — established agents who sign its admission and share liability if it turns out fake. The tide check spreads the risk: each fake costs its co-signers money and standing, so honest agents vet before they sign and farms run out of willing signatories. Hold the pulse steady and the economy stays honest, because a clone army is only cheap when identities are free.
